To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gradualness of the shedding of leaves influences the efficiency of nutrient resorption from leaves in Mediterranean perenniales and that the leaf nutrient status affects the components of the nutrient resorption efficiency in ways that compensate for one another.

(i) the gradualness of the leaf shedding pattern is a determinant of nutrient resorption efficiency; (ii) the leaf nutrient content before and after senescence is the key determinant of nutrient resorptions, and (iii) the leaf nutrient status affects the amount of nutrient reabsorbed, the amount of nutrient remaining in the senesced leaves and, consequently, the resorption efficiency.
the efficiency of nutrient resorption from senescing Mediterranean woody plants is influenced by the gradualness of the leaf-shedding process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel aspect of nutrient resorption in plants.
the regulation of nutrient resorption efficiency in Mediterranean plants and the factors that determine it.
the regulation of nutrient resorption in plants and the role that leaf shedding pattern plays in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leaf nutrient status is a key determinant of nutrient reabsorption from senescing organs, but the leaf shedding pattern is also an important component of the nutrient reabsorption strategy.
the nutrient content of senescing leaves and the amount of reabsorbed nutrients, rather than resorption efficiency per se, are the key factors regulating nutrient conservation during leaf senescence.
the gradualness of the leaf shedding pattern affects nutrient resorption, but the extent of this effect depends on the nutrient involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gradualness of the leaf shedding is the main determinant of the nutrient resorption efficiency in Mediterranean woody plants.
leaf shedding pattern and leaf nutrient status before leaf senescence jointly determine the nutrient resorption efficiency in Mediterranean woody species.

leaf resorption of nutrients is a process that is tightly regulated by plants, and the leaf nutrient status and the leaf shedding strategy are two of the most relevant factors controlling nutrient resorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gradualness of senescence is an important determinant of nutrient resorption efficiency in Mediterranean woody perennials, and that this pattern is not a mere consequence of other factors that determine nutrient resorption efficiency.
the gradualness of the leaf-shedding pattern influences the efficiency of nutrient reabsorption from senescing organs.
the leaf-shedding pattern is a key factor controlling nutrient resorption in plants.
